topic: GPT-6 Astra: The AI That Can Use a Computer
status_convention: VERIFIED | VERIFY | DISPUTED | UNKNOWN (Strict rule: community post claims remain VERIFY until official model card verification)

claims.claim: GPT-6 Astra is a dedicated agentic foundation model optimized for direct computer use, browsing, and OS-level execution.
claims.notes: Described in Sept 3, 2026 Community announcement; awaiting primary model card verification before publication.

claims.claim: GPT-6 Astra supports an active context window of 1,050,000 tokens with a maximum generation output of 128,000 tokens.
claims.notes: Reported in community leak; requires verification against platform.openai.com/docs/models/gpt-6-astra.

claims.claim: Astra API pricing is structured at $10.00 per 1M input tokens and $50.00 per 1M output tokens.
claims.notes: Pending confirmation against official OpenAI pricing tier matrix.

claims.claim: Astra sets state-of-the-art benchmarks on AutomationBench (88.4%) and ScreenSpot Pro (81.2%) for high-resolution desktop GUI control.
claims.notes: Reported in announcement; primary benchmark evaluation methodology requires validation.

claims.claim: On TerminalBench, Astra executes multi-stage shell navigation and sysadmin workflows with 79.6% task completion.
claims.notes: Significant leap over prior terminal agents; pending reproducible harness release.

claims.claim: Astra scores 34.2% on FrontierMath, outperforming all previous frontier models on expert-level original mathematics.
claims.notes: Prior public frontier models scored below 3%; verify whether evaluation included tool-use or python interpreter.

claims.claim: Astra scores 84.5% on ARC-AGI test-public evaluation, demonstrating strong spatial induction.
claims.notes: Verify whether test-time compute scaling or test-private evaluation was utilized.

claims.claim: Traditional LLM chatbots operate on prompt-response loops, whereas computer-use agents execute iterative goal-plan-act-observe-adapt feedback cycles.
claims.notes: Fundamental architectural reality of agentic systems.

claims.claim: In autonomous multi-step software engineering, error propagation in unverified loops remains the primary mode of agent failure in production.
claims.notes: Documented in academic literature and industry deployment post-mortems.

claims.claim: OpenAI positions Astra as incorporating substantial alignment and user-intent guardrails to prevent unintended OS-level destructive actions.
claims.notes: Claimed by OpenAI; real-world boundary testing requires independent verification.
